Metadata.title: LumiLattice
Metadata.description: A collaborative AI scientist for optoelectronic materials discovery.

Home.tagline: A collaborative AI scientist for optoelectronic materials discovery
Home.intro: Explore candidate materials for AR waveguides with Muse Spark. Every number comes from a database or a calculation, with its source.

Language.label: Language
Language.machineTranslated: Machine-translated with Muse Spark. Some terms can be inaccurate.

Status.title: Backend
Status.keyMissing: Meta Model API key missing. Add MODEL_API_KEY to backend/.env.
Status.mpMissing: Materials Project key missing. Add MP_API_KEY to backend/.env.
Status.openAlexMissing: No OpenAlex key: literature search uses a small shared daily budget.
Status.storeMemory: Candidates are kept in memory (lost on restart). Set DATABASE_URL to keep them.

Goal.hint: Set the targets first. Every host and candidate is scored against them, with the evidence behind each verdict.
Goal.note: A band gap of about 3.1 eV puts the absorption edge near 400 nm, the blue end of the visible range.
Goal.title: 1. Research goal

Guide.label: Workflow steps

hint.goal: Set the minimum n (near 550 nm) and band gap, or keep the AR waveguide defaults.
hint.host: Search Materials Project or COD for a known structure, or upload a CIF.
hint.candidate: Replace part of one element's sites in {host}, then read the structural checks.
hint.evidence: Compare {id} with known materials in the Evidence views, then accept, revise, or reject it with a reason.

Guide.allDone: All four steps are done. Revise the candidate, ask the agent for alternatives, or publish it to the registry.
Guide.exampleStory: SrTiO3 has a high n (2.43, measured) but a band gap near the blue edge of the visible range. LaAlO3 has a wider gap but a lower n (2.07). If La replaces 25% of Sr and Al replaces 25% of Ti, does n stay at 2.2 or more while the gap widens? In "{landscape}", the orange box is the candidate's range between the two end members. Then open "{score}" and "{spatial}".

Host.title: 2. Select a host structure
Host.hint: Search Materials Project by formula (SrTiO3, *TiO3), elements (Sr,Ti,O), or ID (mp-5229). Or upload your own CIF.
Host.hintCod: Search the Crystallography Open Database by formula for measured crystal structures (CC0). Credit the original authors.
Host.codCredit: Structures from the Crystallography Open Database (CC0). Please acknowledge the original authors.

Structure.title: 3. Structure
Structure.empty: Select a material or upload a CIF to see its structure.

Candidate.title: 4. Candidates
Candidate.hint: Replace a fraction of one element's sites in {host}. Atom positions stay at the host positions (no relaxation).
Candidate.viewerLegend: Larger atoms: substituted sites. Pink atoms with labels: atoms in the selected check.
Candidate.noHost: This candidate was opened without a host. You can revise it, or select a host to make new candidates.
Candidate.exportNote: The CIF lists every site (P1) with a provenance header. The JSON record adds the goal score, the 3D structure analysis, the data sources, and the caveats.

Evidence.dftComputed: Computed with density functional theory (DFT). Not a measurement.
Evidence.heuristic: Estimated range from similar materials. Not a prediction.
Evidence.hint: Data behind the host and the current candidate: where they sit among known materials, how n changes with wavelength, the per-site numbers behind each check, and the goal score.
Evidence.needSubject: Select a host or a candidate to see this.
Evidence.title: 5. Evidence

Charts.landscapeSubtitle: {measured} materials with measured n, and {computed} JARVIS DFT entries (sampled)
Charts.hiddenPoints: {count} measured materials lie outside the plotted range and are listed only in the table.
Charts.dispersionTitle: Dispersion n(λ) in the visible range
Charts.dispersionSubtitle: Measured bulk curves (refractiveindex.info, median of sources)
Charts.dispersionNote: Curves come only from measured data; nothing is extrapolated beyond each source's wavelength range.
Charts.noCurveAtAll: No measured n(λ) for these materials.
Charts.sitesSubtitle: How far each cation is from its ideal site, by two independent methods
Charts.legendTooSmall: Site too small for the ion (overbonded)
Charts.legendTooLarge: Site too large for the ion (underbonded)
Charts.sitesNote: Shaded zones are the warn (!) and fail (✗) thresholds. Size mismatch uses Shannon radii; bond-valence misfit is the bond-length change that would fix the BVS.

Assessment.clickHint: Select a check to show its atoms.

Agent.title: 6. Research agent (Muse Spark)
Agent.hint: Ask about the host or a candidate. The agent sees the selected host and candidate, uses tools for every number, and remembers this conversation.
Agent.placeholder: Example: Suggest a substitution for SrTiO3 that keeps the band gap wide.
Agent.noToolCalls: No tool calls in this answer. Treat any numbers in it as unverified.

Decision.title: Your decision on {id}
Decision.placeholder: Why? e.g. keep Ti4+ only, avoid toxic elements, try a larger A-site ion
Decision.hint: Accept and Reject are recorded. Modify and Explore are recorded and sent to the agent with your reason.
Decision.modifyHint: The agent revises this candidate from your reason.
Decision.exploreHint: The agent tests up to 2 alternatives from your reason.
Decision.rejectHint: Record that this candidate is not useful, and why.

Optical.computed: DFT gaps and n ({count} entries, JARVIS-DFT)
Optical.computedNote: TBmBJ gaps are usually closer to measured gaps than OptB88vdW. n = sqrt(eps) is a long-wavelength value, not n(550 nm).

Publish.demoNote: Candidates are private by default. In this version, publishing only records your choice and credit; nothing is sent outside LumiLattice.
Publish.consent: I choose to make {id} public, with the credit above.

Relax.title: Relaxation (CHGNet, local install)
Relax.hint: Moves atoms and the cell to lower energy with a machine-learned potential, then runs the same checks. Needs PyTorch, so it runs only in a local install.
Relax.energyNote: ML potential; do not compare with DFT energies

Experiment.title: Measurements
Experiment.hint: Add your own measurement to compare prediction and experiment. LumiLattice records it as given and does not verify it.

Registry.title: 7. Candidate registry
Registry.hint: Every candidate on this server, from the form and from the agent. Select up to {max} to compare.

Spatial.distortionSubtitle: Bond-length distortion index Δ of each substituted site's polyhedron
Spatial.distortionNote: Δ = mean |d − d̄| / d̄ (Baur 1974). The shaded zone (Δ > 0.02) marks clearly distorted polyhedra. The table adds quadratic elongation ⟨λ⟩ and bond-angle variance σ² for octahedra.
Spatial.angleSubtitle: Angles through anions shared by two 6-coordinate cations
Spatial.angleNote: Bending below 180° means the octahedra tilt or buckle. Tilt = (180° − angle)/2, reported only for corner-sharing frameworks such as perovskites.
Spatial.noAngles: No corner-sharing octahedra in this structure.
Spatial.orderingTitle: Where the substituted ions sit: ordering energies
Spatial.orderingSubtitle: {total} arrangements in a {cell} repeat of the candidate cell; {distinct} distinct energies
Spatial.orderingAxis: Ewald energy above the lowest arrangement (meV/atom, point charges)
Spatial.allEqual: Every arrangement has the same Ewald energy (same charges), so this model cannot rank them.
Spatial.sampled: Too many arrangements to list all: a reproducible random sample of 300 is shown.

Literature.title: 8. Literature
Literature.hint: Paper metadata from OpenAlex, Crossref, and arXiv, merged by DOI. LumiLattice does not read full texts.
